An array value (usernames[]=a form encoding) is a legitimate Rails param representation, and Array has no #split method, so NoMethodError → 500 instead of a 4xx. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff; severity is minor since the bundled UI sends a comma string and existing tests only cover string input.

judged_text: add_members calls usernames.split(",") on params.require(:usernames) without any type check, so a request carrying usernames as an array (JSON body {"usernames":["a","b"]} or form field usernames[]=a) raises NoMethodError (undefined method 'split' for Array) and returns a 500. Any consumer of this .json admin API endpoint that naturally passes the usernames as an array gets a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 2xx/4xx; the admin UI (comma-joined string) never triggers it, so the defect stays hidden until an API client appears.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If an API client submits `usernames` as an Array (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` or JSON `{ "usernames": ["a","b"] }`), `split` is undefined on Array and will raise a `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500. The diff contains no type coercion or validation to prevent this.
